Reviewed the diff, `RecurringAllocationsController`, and `DS::Button`'s `merged_opts` beyond what Codex/CodeRabbit already checked (both reported no findings).

**Fix is correct and minimal.** `DS::Button#merged_opts` only applies its `type="button"` default via `merged_opts[:type] ||= "button"` when `href` is blank, so passing `type: "submit"` explicitly here cleanly overrides it (`app/components/DS/button.rb`). As a side benefit, this also restores Turbo's native submit-button disabling during the request — before this change the button wasn't a real submit control at all, so there was no double-submit protection to speak of; now there is, for free, with no extra code needed.

**Tenancy unaffected.** This PR doesn't touch `RecurringAllocationsController#create`, and the existing scoping there (`Current.family.recurring_occurrences`, `ensure_series_writable`, `Current.accessible_entries`) is already correct and untouched.

**Scope call is reasonable.** Deliberately not creating a transaction for the manual-payment path matches the existing `Allocator` design (entry-less allocation) and the help copy; correctly flagged as a product decision rather than silently "fixed."

**One gap worth noting (not a blocker):** the new test (`test/controllers/recurring_occurrences_controller_test.rb`) only asserts the rendered markup has `button[type=submit]`. Since the original bug was specifically a browser/click behavior issue (Enter submitted, click didn't), a markup assertion can't fully prove the regression is fixed end-to-end — it would pass even if some other handler intercepted the click. There's no existing system test covering this drawer's manual-payment flow to extend, and the markup-only style matches this file's existing tests, so this is consistent with current conventions rather than a deviation — but a short system test (visit occurrence, click "Record payment", assert the allocation/flash) would be the stronger regression guard here if the team wants one.

No DS/token/i18n/icon convention violations in the diff — it's a one-attribute change reusing the existing `DS::Button` call and unchanged `t(".record_payment")` label.
